$comment: WildLens v2 Wildlife Event Schema — rough draft for Nikunj to validate. Every field marked REQUIRED must be present; OPTIONAL fields may be null.

definitions.poaching: Illegal killing, trapping, or trade of wildlife or wildlife parts
definitions.hwc: Human-wildlife conflict — attacks on humans, crop raids, property damage, retaliatory killing
definitions.mortality: Animal death from natural causes, disease, accident (train/vehicle), or unknown cause
definitions.sighting: Notable or rare sighting of a species, first record for an area
definitions.discovery: New species described, new range record, new behaviour documented
definitions.conservation_action: Proactive management — translocations, camera traps, drone surveys, reserve notifications, ex-situ conservation
definitions.habitat_threat: Mining, forest fires, encroachment, road/infra projects affecting wildlife habitat
definitions.policy: Government orders, court rulings, legislation, ESZ notifications, budget allocations
definitions.research: Population surveys, censuses, ecological studies, camera trap results published

event_date.note: Best estimate of when the event occurred (not when reported)

event_date_precision.note: How precise is event_date? Most news articles allow 'exact' or 'week'

reported_date.note: Date of earliest article covering this event

species.type: array — one entry per species mentioned

count.note: Number of individual animals, if known

place_name.note: Most specific place name that can be confidently extracted

definitions.point: Specific PA, town, forest range, or named locality (±10km)
definitions.state: State centroid only — could not determine finer location
definitions.region: Multi-state geographic region (e.g. Western Ghats, Northeast India)

inside_pa.note: Set by PostGIS spatial join in Phase 2

nearest_pa_name.note: Name of nearest PA if location is outside any PA

outcome_summary.note: 1-2 sentence plain English description of what happened and result
outcome_summary.example: Wild elephant fatally attacked a farmer in Wayanad. Forest department took responsibility for victim's children.

human_casualties.note: Number of humans killed or seriously injured

definitions.critical: Human death, large-scale habitat loss, critically endangered species directly threatened
definitions.high: Human injury, significant habitat damage, multiple animals killed, large fire/encroachment
definitions.medium: Property damage, smaller incidents, policy/administrative actions with medium conservation impact
definitions.low: No immediate harm, awareness events, minor incidents, positive news

source_articles.type: array — all articles covering this event
source_articles.note: Multiple articles = same event as identified by deduplication step

item.headline: string (required)
item.is_primary: boolean — which article has the most complete information (required)

is_valid_wildlife_event.note: False for false positives that passed keyword filter (e.g. lone-wolf terrorism, Shigellosis)

needs_review.note: Set true when confidence is low or fields conflict

review_notes.note: Free text for annotator or pipeline to explain uncertainty

outcome.outcome_summary: Wild elephant fatally attacked a 65-year-old man in Wayanad. Forest department took responsibility for the victim's two children.

source_articles.headline: Wild elephant attack claims 65-year-old man in Kerala's Wayanad
Kerala wild elephant attack: forest department takes responsibility for victim's children

regulatory_data_track.$comment: PLANNING NOTE (added 2026-06-16): A third data ingestion track alongside RSS news — pulling from structured government/legal portals. Higher confidence than NLP extraction. Enables predictive threat detection and project lifecycle tracking.

data_gov_in.access: Free with API key — register at data.gov.in. Python: pip install datagovindia
data_gov_in.license: Open Government Data License India (free, attribution required)
data_gov_in.example_code: from datagovindia import DataGovIndia; d = DataGovIndia(); d.get_data('resource-id')

relevant_datasets.environmental_clearance_parivesh: 50,000+ EC approvals from PARIVESH 2.0 — resource at data.gov.in/catalog/environmental-clearance-granted-parivesh-20
relevant_datasets.wildlife_sanctuaries: Number and area of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
relevant_datasets.forest_area: State-wise recorded forest area and legal status

data_gov_in.limitations: EC data only (Environment Clearance). Forest Clearance (FC) and Wildlife Clearance (WL) data is NOT on data.gov.in — must scrape PARIVESH portal directly for those.
data_gov_in.priority: HIGH — best structured source for environment clearance data, official, free

ecourts_akshit_api.access: Free for non-commercial use. API key required.
features: Covers District Courts, High Courts, Supreme Court
ecourts_akshit_api.use_for_wildlens: Search Wildlife Protection Act 1972 cases, Forest Conservation Act 1980 cases, track poaching prosecution outcomes
ecourts_akshit_api.priority: HIGH — broadest court coverage including District Courts where most wildlife cases begin

features: Search cases by Act type (✅ working)
Cases by case number / FIR (🚧 in development)
Orders by case number (🚧 in development)
limitations: High Courts only — not District Courts
ecourts_openjustice.use_for_wildlens: Filter by Act: Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Act, Environment Protection Act. Pull HC orders for wildlife/forest cases.
ecourts_openjustice.priority: MEDIUM — complementary to Akshit API; useful for bulk HC case retrieval by Act

PARIVESH.access: Public portal; FC data available as Excel download; WL data NOT available as structured download
PARIVESH.workaround: Scrape portal OR use data.gov.in for EC data. For FC and WL, a researcher (vjjan91/Environmental-Clearances on GitHub) scraped the portal 2000-2020 — their methodology can be replicated.
data_available: Area of forest to be diverted (hectares)
For Wildlife Clearance: species affected sometimes listed
PARIVESH.priority: HIGH — most important source for predictive threat detection, but requires scraping

NGT.access: Public PDFs. Third-party: enviroannotations.com indexes NGT orders and may be scrapeable.
NGT.pipeline_required: Web scrape order list → download PDF → pdfplumber/pymupdf text extraction → NLP for location/species/outcome
data_available: PA / forest / species named in order
Order type: stay / penalty / remediation / dismissed
NGT.priority: MEDIUM — high value per order but requires PDF pipeline. Implement after PARIVESH and eCourts.

WCCB.access: Annual reports (PDF). Third-party: dataful.in has year+state-wise wildlife crime cases as a dataset.
WCCB.limitations: No live data feed. Annual reports lag by 1-2 years. Not viable as a real-time source.
WCCB.use_for_wildlens: Calibration and benchmarking only — use WCCB annual data to validate poaching event counts extracted from news+court sources.
WCCB.priority: LOW — reference/validation only, not a live ingestion source

new_event_types.clearance_application: Forest/environment clearance filed with MoEFCC via PARIVESH — represents a FUTURE threat
new_event_types.clearance_granted: Stage-1 or Stage-2 forest/environment clearance approved
new_event_types.clearance_rejected: Application rejected by FAC (Forest Advisory Committee) or MoEFCC
new_event_types.clearance_conditional: Approved with mitigation conditions (list conditions as outcome_summary)
new_event_types.ngt_order: NGT issues an order — stay, penalty, remediation direction, or case dismissed
new_event_types.court_judgment: High Court or Supreme Court judgment on a wildlife/forest case

source_type.note: Determines which extraction pipeline was used and expected confidence level

regulatory.type: object — present only when source_type is regulatory_document / court_order / ngt_order

fields.case_number: string — PARIVESH project ID, NGT case number, or CNR number
fields.case_status: enum: pending | stage1_cleared | stage2_cleared | approved | rejected | conditional | challenged | stayed | decided | appealed
fields.project_name: string — official project name from the application
fields.project_proponent: string — company/government agency filing the application
fields.clearance_type: enum: FC | EC | WL | combined (Forest Clearance, Environment Clearance, Wildlife Clearance)
fields.forest_area_ha: float — area of forest to be diverted in hectares (from PARIVESH application)
fields.verdict_summary: string — 1-2 sentence plain English of the decision
fields.next_hearing_date: YYYY-MM-DD or null — if case is still pending
fields.document_url: string — link to the official order/application PDF

lifecycle_example.description: A single mining project in a wildlife corridor can generate multiple events across time, all linkable by project_name or case_number

timeline.note: PARIVESH entry — first alert before any news coverage
Conservationists learn of application, protest begins

what_this_enables: Predictive threat detection — flag forest clearance applications in wildlife corridors BEFORE construction starts
Project lifecycle tracking — link regulatory event → news coverage → on-ground impact into one timeline
Regulatory lag measurement — how long between clearance application and news coverage? Between approval and NGT challenge?
Compliance monitoring — cross-reference 'clearance_conditional' events with later news to see if conditions were met
Academic novelty — integrating regulatory + news + field data into a unified ecological intelligence model is not done anywhere currently

forest_cover_change_track.$comment: PLANNING NOTE (added 2026-06-16): A fourth data track — spatial/raster analysis of forest cover change. Not events in the traditional sense but continuous spatial intelligence that grounds all other tracks in physical reality.

three_layer_model.description: The core analytical framework for ecological intelligence. Each layer answers a different question. The GAPS between layers are where the intelligence lives.
three_layer_model.layer_1_regulatory: What was AUTHORIZED — PARIVESH clearances, NGT orders, court judgments
three_layer_model.layer_2_events: What was REPORTED — news articles, court proceedings, poaching arrests
three_layer_model.layer_3_ground_truth: What ACTUALLY HAPPENED — satellite-derived forest cover change

gap_analysis.L1_exists_L3_confirms: Authorized deforestation — clearance was acted upon
gap_analysis.L3_loss_no_L1: ILLEGAL ENCROACHMENT — forest cleared with no clearance ever filed. High-priority alert.
gap_analysis.L1_granted_no_L3_loss: Clearance not yet acted on — continue monitoring
gap_analysis.L2_reports_L3_confirms: Validated event — high confidence, use for gold standard
gap_analysis.L3_loss_no_L2: UNDERREPORTED DEGRADATION — satellite detected loss that never made the news
gap_analysis.L1_exists_no_L2_or_L3: Pending threat — clearance filed but not yet in news or on ground

ecological_metrics.forest_cover_area_ha: Total forest cover within a polygon (PA, corridor, district) at a given date
ecological_metrics.annual_loss_ha: Hectares lost per year — from GFW tree cover loss dataset
ecological_metrics.fragmentation_index: Patch size distribution — smaller isolated patches indicate habitat degradation
ecological_metrics.edge_density: Perimeter-to-area ratio — high edge density = degraded interior habitat quality
ecological_metrics.corridor_width_m: Minimum width of a wildlife corridor at its narrowest point — pinch point detection
ecological_metrics.corridor_connectivity: Least-cost path analysis — is the corridor still traversable by target species?
ecological_metrics.ndvi_trend: Vegetation health trend from Sentinel-2 — detects degradation before outright deforestation
ecological_metrics.forest_cover_pct_change: % change relative to baseline year (e.g. 2000 or 2010)
ecological_metrics.canopy_cover_pct: Canopy closure within the polygon — from GFW tree canopy cover layer

spatial_correlations.hwc_vs_forest_loss: Spatial correlation between HWC events and forest loss in adjacent areas — losing forest drives wildlife into human settlements
spatial_correlations.poaching_vs_forest_fragmentation: More forest edge = more poaching access = higher poaching event density at edges
spatial_correlations.new_species_vs_intact_forest: Discovery events cluster in areas with high canopy cover — prioritise for protection

corridor_stress_vs_corridor_integrity.stress_index: Events-based — frequency of incidents in corridor (from news track)
corridor_stress_vs_corridor_integrity.integrity_index: Area-based — physical width and connectivity of corridor (from remote sensing track)
corridor_stress_vs_corridor_integrity.combined_insight: High stress + declining integrity = corridor in active collapse. High stress + stable integrity = corridor under pressure but intact. Low stress + declining integrity = underreported degradation.

primary_spatial_source.$comment: Global Forest Watch is the primary source for ALL spatial forest cover analysis. It consolidates what would otherwise require multiple sources.
primary_spatial_source.api_type: REST API — POST polygon GeoJSON + SQL query
primary_spatial_source.access: Free with account and API key (expires annually)

umd_tree_cover_loss.query_example: SELECT umd_tree_cover_loss__year, SUM(area__ha) as loss_ha FROM results GROUP BY year

umd_tree_cover_loss_by_driver.description: Attributes loss to: commodity agriculture, shifting agriculture, forestry, wildfire, urbanization
covers: attribution — distinguishes legal clearing from wildfire from encroachment

integrated_deforestation_alerts.description: Near-real-time alerts (GLAD-L, GLAD-S2, RADD) — weekly cadence, 10–30m resolution

primary_forest.description: Intact primary forest layer — highest conservation value areas
covers: primary forest loss — most severe category of habitat degradation

tree_cover_as_raster.description: Forest cover as continuous raster — can be used to compute spatial metrics
tree_cover_as_raster.how: Download GeoTIFF for corridor polygon → compute patch statistics with rasterio/scipy → narrowest contiguous forest = corridor width

secondary_sources.fsi_isfr: Official GoI numbers for paper citations — no API, biennial PDF. Use to cross-validate GFW numbers with India government methodology.
secondary_sources.nikunj_forest_cover: Downversioned FSI/MoEFCC data already available — load as PostGIS raster for India-specific baseline where GFW resolution is insufficient.
secondary_sources.isro_bhuvan_wms: LULC classification (what land use replaced forest) — WMS at bhuvan-vec2.nrsc.gov.in/bhuvan/wms, no auth needed. Complements GFW with land-use type context.

new_event_types.forest_cover_loss_alert: GFW deforestation alert fired within a PA, corridor, or PA buffer zone — triggers cross-check against PARIVESH and news
new_event_types.corridor_integrity_change: Computed quarterly — corridor width or connectivity drops below threshold
new_event_types.illegal_encroachment_detected: Forest loss confirmed by satellite with no corresponding PARIVESH clearance in the same area and period
new_event_types.forest_cover_report: Periodic (annual/biennial) summary of forest cover change for a PA or corridor — not a discrete event but a monitoring output

implementation_sequence: 1. Load PA boundary shapefiles into PostGIS
2. For each PA: query GFW API with boundary polygon → get annual loss 2001–2024 → store as baseline time series
3. Load corridor polygons → compute corridor width and connectivity metrics using PostGIS
4. Load Nikunj's forest cover data as raster baseline
5. Set up weekly GFW deforestation alert polling → alert fired in PA buffer → auto-create forest_cover_loss_alert event → cross-check PARIVESH for that location
6. Quarterly: re-run corridor integrity metrics → compare to previous quarter → flag degradation

reference_spatial_datasets.$comment: Static reference layers loaded once into PostGIS. Not polled — used for spatial joins and corridor/PA enrichment. Additions 2026-06-16: WTI corridors, WII/NWIS, GBIF.

wti_elephant_corridors.source: Wildlife Trust of India — Right of Passage project
wti_elephant_corridors.publication: Right of Passage: Elephant Corridors of India, 2nd Edition (2017) + 2023 MoEF update
attributes_per_corridor: connecting_PAs (two PA names the corridor links)
wti_elephant_corridors.gis_data_availability: No public shapefile download. PDF has corridor maps with arrows on forest cover raster. To get GIS data: (1) contact WTI project lead Upasana Ganguly directly, OR (2) manually digitize from the 183-page PDF into PostGIS, OR (3) MoEF may have shapefiles — file RTI.
use_for_wildlens_v2: Primary corridor reference layer — replace the hand-coded corridor_name field in the event schema with a PostGIS lookup against the 101 WTI corridors
Enables corridor_stress_index: count events within each of the 101 named corridors
Enables pinch-point analysis: measure current GFW corridor width at the WTI-defined narrowest points
Attribute linking: article mentions 'Sigur corridor' → look up WTI record → get connecting PAs (Mudumalai ↔ Nagarahole), state (Tamil Nadu), status (partially obstructed)
wti_elephant_corridors.action_required: Contact WTI for shapefile or digitize from PDF. This is a one-time setup task.

wii_data.source: Wildlife Institute of India (MoEFCC autonomous body)

national_wildlife_information_system_nwi.access: No public API. Request via WII directly or through data.gov.in. Some PA boundary shapefiles may be on WDPA (World Database of Protected Areas).
national_wildlife_information_system_nwi.priority: HIGH — PA boundaries are needed for PostGIS spatial joins. Use WDPA (protectedplanet.net) as the public alternative if WII data is not accessible.

tiger_census_reports.cadence: Every 4 years — All India Tiger Estimation
tiger_census_reports.access: PDF reports only. No API. Distribution grid maps sometimes released as shapefiles.
tiger_census_reports.use_for_wildlens: Baseline tiger population per landscape — contextualize poaching/mortality events against the population at risk

m_stripes.description: Monitoring System for Tigers – Intensive Protection and Ecological Status. Used by all 54 tiger reserves for daily beat-level patrol logging.
m_stripes.access: NOT public. Internal government system. Data would need MoEFCC data-sharing agreement.
m_stripes.note: If Nikunj has any WII affiliation, this is the most granular tiger monitoring dataset in existence — worth pursuing through institutional channels.

herbarium_via_gbif.description: 4,322 digitized plant specimens from WII herbarium, published to GBIF
herbarium_via_gbif.use_for_wildlens: Limited — plant specimens. Useful for habitat characterisation (what species grow in a PA) but not for wildlife events.

research_reports.note: Rich source for species distribution studies, corridor assessments, HWC reports — useful as background reading, not as a data feed.

wdpa_alternative.note: For PA boundaries specifically, the World Database of Protected Areas (WDPA) is the public alternative to NWIS. Monthly updates, global, includes all Indian PAs with boundary polygons.
wdpa_alternative.api: WDPA has a REST API (iatistandard.org/protectedplanet). Also available as monthly shapefile download. Free for non-commercial use.
wdpa_alternative.priority: HIGH — Use WDPA shapefiles to populate the PostGIS PA layer if NWIS is not accessible.

gbif.what_it_is: Aggregated occurrence records from museums, research institutions, citizen science (iNaturalist, eBird, etc.) and government datasets. For India: millions of geo-referenced species observations.
gbif.access: Free. Requires free account for bulk downloads. Search/count API needs no authentication.

key_queries.count_species_in_india: from pygbif import occurrences as occ; occ.count(country='IN', taxonKey=<gbif_taxon_key>)

gbif.india_data_volume: ~40 million occurrence records for India across all taxa. Key publishers: iNaturalist, eBird (Cornell), Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), ZSI, BSI, WII.

use_for_wildlens_v2.species_range_priors: ★ NOVEL — Species occurrence density map from GBIF. When NER extracts two possible location candidates for a tiger article, score each by GBIF tiger occurrence density within 50km. Higher density = more ecologically plausible = pick that location. This is the species-constrained toponym disambiguation contribution.
use_for_wildlens_v2.species_presence_baseline: For each PA in PostGIS, build a species checklist from GBIF occurrences within the PA boundary. Use as baseline for 'first recorded sighting' detection — if an event mentions a species in a PA where GBIF has no prior record, it is a discovery event.
use_for_wildlens_v2.iucn_range_cross_check: GBIF occurrence data can approximate IUCN range maps for India-specific taxa where IUCN shapefiles are not granular enough.
use_for_wildlens_v2.citizen_science_events: iNaturalist observations flow through GBIF — high-quality geo-referenced sightings from the field. Can supplement news-based sighting events.
use_for_wildlens_v2.species_trend_analysis: Year-over-year GBIF record count by species and PA — rough proxy for population trend (with caveats about observation effort)

caveats: Observation bias — more records near roads, cities, and accessible areas. Dense GBIF records ≠ actually more animals there.
Coordinate uncertainty varies wildly — some records have 1m precision, others 100km. Always filter by coordinateUncertaintyInMeters < 10000 for spatial analysis.
basisOfRecord matters — PRESERVED_SPECIMEN may be decades old. Filter to HUMAN_OBSERVATION for recent presence data.
Citizen science records are generally good quality but unverified. BNHS and ZSI records are expert-verified.

notes_for_nikunj.fields_to_add: Add any fields here that you think are missing from an ecological standpoint
notes_for_nikunj.fields_to_remove: Cross out any fields that are not practically extractable from news text
notes_for_nikunj.severity_calibration: The severity enum definitions above are my first pass — adjust thresholds based on your ecological judgement
notes_for_nikunj.location_precision: The point/district/state hierarchy may need a fourth level — e.g. 'forest_range' between point and district
notes_for_nikunj.species_handling: Articles sometimes mention multiple species (e.g. elephant + leopard in same corridor). Should all species be listed, or only the primary one?
notes_for_nikunj.event_type_gaps: Are there event types I am missing that you encounter in the field? E.g. 'zoonosis', 'flood_displacement', 'court_order_specific'?
notes_for_nikunj.regulatory_track_priority: The regulatory data track (PARIVESH + NGT + eCourts) is architecturally separate from news ingestion but feeds the same event store. PARIVESH is the highest priority source — it provides structured location data and represents threats not yet in the news.
notes_for_nikunj.wti_corridor_action: WTI elephant corridor shapefile is the single most valuable static layer for v2. If you have any WTI contacts, the fastest path is to email the Right of Passage project lead directly and ask for the GeoJSON/shapefile — they may share for research purposes.
notes_for_nikunj.gbif_novel_contribution: The species-constrained toponym disambiguation (using GBIF occurrence density to score NER location candidates) is marked ★ NOVEL in the schema. This is a genuine methodological contribution worth calling out explicitly in the paper — no prior system has used GBIF ranges as a location disambiguation prior for wildlife news NLP.
notes_for_nikunj.wii_mstripes: If you have any institutional connection to WII or any tiger reserve, M-STrIPES data would be transformative — it is the only daily-resolution ground-truth dataset for tiger movement and patrol coverage. Worth pursuing through a formal data-sharing request.
